title: Sharpness-Aware Gradient Matching for Domain Generalization
main_claims: SAM and its variants do not always converge to flat minima with low loss, because the perturbed loss Lp(θ) is not always a reliable sharpness measure.
SAGM simultaneously minimizes empirical risk, perturbed loss, and surrogate gap by implicitly aligning gradients of L(θ) and Lp(θ), achieving better convergence to flat low-loss minima.
SAGM consistently outperforms SAM, GSAM, and conventional DG methods on five DomainBed benchmarks without increasing computational cost.
methodology: SAGM adds a gradient matching term to SAM's objective, requiring that the gradient directions of L(θ) and Lp(θ) remain aligned; this is achieved by minimizing L(θ) + Lp(θ − α∇L(θ)). Experiments follow the DomainBed evaluation protocol on PACS, VLCS, OfficeHome, TerraIncognita, and DomainNet, using ResNet-50 pretrained on ImageNet. Local sharpness is assessed by measuring the surrogate gap h_ρ(θ) across varying radii ρ.
key_results: SAGM achieves 66.1% average OOD accuracy on DomainBed, compared to 64.5% for SAM and 65.1% for GSAM.
SAGM outperforms ERM by +2.2% average across five benchmarks.
SAGM finds flatter minima than SAM and GSAM across all target domains of PACS as measured by the surrogate gap h_ρ(θ).
SAGM+Mixstyle achieves 87.2% out-of-domain on PACS, a further improvement over SAGM alone (86.2%).
limitations: Experiments use ResNet-50 with ImageNet pretraining; results on smaller models (e.g. ResNet-18 from scratch) are not reported in the main paper.
Sharpness analysis uses the surrogate gap measure (SAM-style neighborhood loss) rather than Hessian eigenvalues; only correlational evidence linking sharpness to OOD accuracy.
Does not include CIFAR-C/ImageNet-C benchmarks; domain generalization benchmarks (PACS etc.) use different domain-shift types than corruption benchmarks.
relevance_to_rq: Directly relevant: provides a SAM variant with tighter flatness guarantees and demonstrates that flatter minima (lower surrogate gap) correlate with higher OOD accuracy on DG benchmarks, supporting the hypothesis that SAM's OOD gains are linked to loss geometry. Also references SWAD as a related flat-minima method.

key_quotes.text: minimizing Lp(θ) is not guaranteed to converge to flat minimum regions
key_quotes.context: Motivation for SAGM: SAM's perturbed loss is not a reliable sharpness measure

key_quotes.text: SAGM achieves an average performance improvement of 1.3% over ERM+SAM, which illustrates the importance of gradient matching in our designed objective function
key_quotes.context: Ablation result quantifying the contribution of the gradient-matching term

key_quotes.text: SAGM finds the flattest minima in all experiments
key_quotes.context: Local sharpness analysis showing SAGM surpasses SAM and GSAM in finding flat regions
